title: Dungeon hosts never run the 8-hour enemy-alert decay
claim: decayEnemyAlert's only caller in src/ is shared.createPlayerTicker.tick (shared.js:746), and neither dungeon host builds a ticker: dungeonContext's frame body calls tickPlayerMinutes directly (:2100) and its rest advance uses claimMagicRounds/runMagicRoundsFor (:953-963); nothing calls decayEnemyAlert. DFU decays the alert in PlayerEntity.Update in every context (PlayerEntity.cs:381-384). The port raises it whenever a foe has the player in sight (:2233) and clears it only when the detecting foe dies (:1847), so underground it only goes up. Its sole consumer is the dungeon resting spawn roll (encounters.js rollDungeon: alert -> 1/36 per rested minute; no alert -> never).
consequence: Resting in a dungeon 8+ hours after last enemy contact (or when the sighting foe was not killed): DFU rolls no interruption spawns; the port rolls 1-in-36 per rested minute forever, breaking long dungeon rests with spawns classic would not mint.

title: Exterior corpse batches never culled, freed, or cleared on teleport - unbounded growth
claim: Both exterior pools keep every corpse forever: exteriorFoes' splice spares corpses (:401), the cull (:286) skips dead foes (:252), and corpseBatches (:60/:214/:486) has no removal path - batches() draws every corpse every frame. cityGuards.js is identical (:95/:290/:445; :248-256 says guards[] cannot be pruned). The teleport core (world.js:1478-1500) never touches either pool. DFU tracks exterior corpse markers as loose objects (GameObjectHelper.cs:839) and destroys them when out of range or on any teleport (CollectLooseObjects :1040-1055; ClearStreamingWorld :993 from InitWorld :584). The port ported that law for player drops (droppedLoot.collectPixel cites :1040-1052) but not for corpses.
consequence: Every kill permanently adds a VAO+buffers and an array entry drawn every frame; corpses from towns you fast-travelled away from still render and probe loot AABBs. GPU memory and draw time grow without bound over a session.

title: applyWorld never removes live foes beyond the snapshot; rewound CreateFoe re-spawns duplicates
claim: DFU's load rebuilds the scene and instantiates exactly the saved enemy set (RestoreEnemyData creates one object per saved record; enemies born after the save are gone with the rebuild). The port's applyWorld (dungeonContext.js:1768-1770) patches foes in place by index over w.foes only - a live foes[] entry at an index past the snapshot's length is left standing untouched. Meanwhile restoreSessionState rewinds CreateFoe's spawnCounter/lastSpawnTime (quest/actions.js:1980 saveShape), so the restored action's wave budget no longer accounts for the survivor.
consequence: Quicksave, let a quest wave (create foe) spawn, quickload: the post-save wave stays alive AND the rewound CreateFoe counter spawns it again - duplicate quest foes after a backward load, where DFU's rebuild-from-save yields exactly the saved population.

title: Witness/countdown half of spawnCityGuards has no production caller
claim: The non-immediate arm (cityGuards.js:196-238; countdown consumed :325-328) is called with immediate=false only by test/cityguards.test.js:81. Both hosts pass true only (world.js:1030, exterior.js:625) and the quest SpawnCityGuards action is a pended guard pattern (systems/quest/actions.js:2672). DFU's false-mode callers are PlayerEntity.cs:500-503 (LegalRep < -10, 5% per game-hour, Criminal_Conspiracy) and :507-510 (banished flag, 10%); grep of src/ finds no port counterpart of either arm.
consequence: The witness law - civilians seeing a crime, guard NPCs converting on sight, guards arriving after a 5-10s countdown - and passive guard responses to low-legal-rep/banished characters never run in the shipped game.

verify.reason: cityGuards.js:196-238 (witness arm) runs only with immediate=false; both hosts pass true only (world.js:1030, exterior.js:625), sole false-caller is test/cityguards.test.js:81. In DFU, SpawnCityGuards(false) (PlayerEntity.cs:621) is reached ONLY from the periodic rolls at :500-510 (LegalRep<-10 5%/min, banished-flag 10%/min); every other DFU crime site calls true directly. Grep of src/ finds no port implementation of that periodic roll; arrestFlow.js:159-160 flags it pending. So the port's only match for DFU's false-callers is absent, leaving the witness code dead.

title: Standalone dungeon fly-cam is dead code: `else if (!held)` tests the imported input helper
claim: dungeon.js:427 gates the fly-cam WASD block with `} else if (!held) {`, but `held` there is the FUNCTION imported from ui/input.js (:33, used as held(keys,'Jump') at :367) - always truthy, so !held is always false and the branch never runs. Sibling hosts use a bare `} else {` (exterior.js:1545, world.js:3215). worldModes.js:2744's comment shows the drift: an old dungeon.js line used a local boolean `held` later renamed overlayHeld (:353), leaving this stale reference resolving to the import. Port-internal bug, no C# counterpart; no test pins it.
consequence: With ?dungeon&fly (the file's own documented mode, :103-105) or ?shot without probe pokes, WASD/Shift never moves the camera - the fly-cam is frozen at spawn; look still works. Shot-mode probes (__move/__pose) still function.

verify.reason: dungeon.js:33 imports `held` as a function; at :427 the fly-cam branch is gated `} else if (!held) {` where `held` is that function reference (always truthy), so `!held` is always false and the fly-cam body (:428-432) never runs. Sibling host exterior.js:1545 uses a bare `} else {` for the identical block, confirming intended shape. Port-internal dead code.

title: A failed night-panorama build permanently wedges the sky controller's pending guard
claim: createSkyController.use(): `pending = key; ... buildPanorama(...).then(apply)` (shared.js:178,194) has no .catch, and the NIGHT branch of buildPanorama (:137-149) awaits fetchBytes for the NITE IMG and its palette with no try/catch - unlike its day-sky sibling (:152-162), which catches and degrades to the gradient. On a rejected fetch, apply never runs, pending stays equal to that key, and every later use() for the same key returns at :177 (`key === pending`) - never retried, plus an unhandled rejection. Recovery only when a DIFFERENT key is requested (dawn). DFU reads local files and has no one-shot guard to wedge.
consequence: One failed NITE fetch at nightfall (lean data set, transient IndexedDB/network error) freezes the sky on the last day frame for the whole night with no retry.

verify.reason: shared.js:136-149 night-branch buildPanorama has no try/catch on its two fetchBytes calls, unlike the day branch (:150-163) which catches and degrades. use() (:171-195) sets pending=key (:178) then `buildPanorama(...).then(apply)` (:194) with no .catch; pending is only cleared inside apply() (:191/:181), which never runs on rejection. Grep confirms no other writer resets pending. No test covers createSkyController. DFU's LoadVanillaNightSky (DaggerfallSky.cs:565-604) is a sync local file read, no async failure path - matches claim DFU has no equivalent wedge.

title: Dungeon drowning deals zero damage: 3-arg call into the local 1-arg hurtPlayer wrapper
claim: breathTick's drowned arm calls hurtPlayer(playerEntity, playerEntity.health, { bypassShield: true }) (:2045), but the LOCAL hurtPlayer (:1030-1032) takes ONE arg (dmg) and forwards hurtEntity(playerEntity, dmg). So dmg = the playerEntity OBJECT; playerEntity.js:97's guard `if (!(dmg > 0)) return false` sees object>0 -> NaN -> false, and returns having done nothing. The call shape was copied from world.js:637 where hurtPlayer IS the 3-arg import (world.js:110); here the import is aliased hurtEntity (:26) and shadowed by the wrapper. The :2043 comment claims this exact bug class was already review-fixed.
consequence: PlayerEntity.cs:339-340 does SetHealth(0) at 0 breath; in the port a player out of breath underwater in a dungeon takes no damage at all - drowning can never hurt or kill. Only breathStep's unit test pins the systems half; no test pins this host call.

verify.reason: dungeonContext.js:26 imports the real 3-arg hurtPlayer as hurtEntity, but :1030-1032 locally redefines hurtPlayer(dmg) (1 arg), shadowing it file-wide. The drowned arm (:2045) calls hurtPlayer(playerEntity, playerEntity.health, {bypassShield:true}) against this 1-arg wrapper, so dmg=playerEntity (object). playerEntity.js:97's guard `if (!(dmg>0)) return false` sees NaN comparison -> false -> returns doing nothing. test/breath.test.js only pins systems/breath.js, not this host call. Confirmed: dungeon drowning to 0 breath deals zero damage.

title: Runtime-spawned dungeon foes (rest encounters, quest CreateFoe) never get spell lists or a caster
claim: assignEnemySpells + EnemyCaster minting runs ONCE over the load-time foes array (:691-696). _spawnEncounter (:913-928) and spawnQuestFoe (:630-636) call buildFoeAt (:479), which never assigns spells; the frame loop's cast arm reads f.caster (:2312) - undefined for those foes. DFU's SetEnemyCareer assigns the spell lists on EVERY spawn (EnemyEntity.cs:350-386) and SetEnemySpells also pins magicka = 10*level+100 and four magic skills to 80 (:453-461); the port's makeEnemyEntity does neither. The port's own exterior pool assigns per-spawn inside its build path (exteriorFoes.js:107-109), so this host is the odd one out.
consequence: An Imp, Orc Shaman, Vampire, Lich, or CastsMagic class enemy spawned by a dungeon rest interruption or placed by a quest never casts a single spell and has no caster magicka pool; the same enemy at a load-time marker, or spawned outdoors, casts normally.

verify.reason: dungeonContext.js:691-696 assigns spells/casters in a ONE-TIME loop over `foes` run once during setup, after the load loop (:623); buildFoeAt itself (:479-622, read in full) never calls assignEnemySpells or mints EnemyCaster. spawnQuestFoe (:630-636) and _spawnEncounter (:913-928) push new records via buildFoeAt AFTER that one-time loop, so late-spawned foes never get spells; frame loop's cast check (:2312, f.caster&&...) is always false for them. DFU's SetEnemyCareer (EnemyEntity.cs:248-386,453-461) runs the spell/magicka assignment on every entity construction, i.e. every spawn.
